cards: The scholar Jules Oppert gives the rediscovered language the name Sumerian
A statue of King Ibbit-Lim identifies Tell Mardikh as Ebla
Bedouin find a statue on Tell Hariri, leading to French excavations
Humban-nikash I fights Sargon II of Assyria at the Battle of Der
Sennacherib's son Ashur-nadin-shumi is handed to Elam and dies in captivity
Byblos passes under the Achaemenid Empire
Byblos submits to Alexander the Great and its king joins the siege of Tyre
Cyrus the Great takes Babylon and records his conquest in Akkadian on the Cyrus Cylinder
Four scholars independently translate an Assyrian inscription, proving the decipherment
The Chicago Assyrian Dictionary is completed after nearly ninety years of work
King Uperi of Dilmun sends gifts to Sargon II of Assyria
Dilmun passes with Babylonia to the Achaemenid Empire
Danish expedition under P.V. Glob and Geoffrey Bibby begins excavations
Adad-nirari II launches the Neo-Assyrian revival
Tiglath-pileser III takes the throne and reorganises army and provinces
Samaria falls and the population of the Kingdom of Israel is deported
Esarhaddon conquers Egypt, bringing the empire to its greatest extent
Babylonians and Medes destroy the Assyrian capital Nineveh
Ashur-uballit II fails to retake Harran and vanishes from the record
Hammurabi defeats an Elamite-led coalition, launching his conquests
Hammurabi conquers Larsa, bringing all southern Mesopotamia under his rule
Hammurabi conquers his former ally Mari
Hammurabi dies; his son Samsu-iluna soon faces widespread revolt
Ugaritic troops fight for the Hittites at the Battle of Kadesh
A farmer’s discovery of a tomb at Minet el-Beida leads to excavations
Claude Schaeffer begins excavating Ras Shamra
Muwatalli II fights Ramesses II at Kadesh, perhaps the largest chariot battle of antiquity
An eclipse ends the war with Media; the Halys becomes the frontier
Ardashir I founds the Sasanian Empire, under which Zoroastrianism becomes the state religion
The last Sasanian king, Yazdegerd III, is killed after the Arab conquest of Iran
The Parsi Dadabhai Naoroji becomes the first Asian elected to the British House of Commons
Eliezer Ben-Yehuda settles in Jerusalem and begins his campaign to revive spoken Hebrew
The British Mandate for Palestine recognises Hebrew as an official language beside English and Arabic
The first Dead Sea Scrolls, including the oldest known manuscripts of the Hebrew Bible, are found near Qumran
Israel founds the Academy of the Hebrew Language
The Babylonians destroy Jerusalem and the First Temple and take many Judeans into exile
The Second Temple is completed in Jerusalem after the return from exile, by the traditional date
The Romans destroy Jerusalem and the Second Temple at the end of the Jewish revolt
The Jews are expelled from Spain
The State of Israel is founded, three years after the end of the Holocaust
Ahab fights Shalmaneser III of Assyria at the Battle of Qarqar
Tiglath-pileser III annexes Galilee and Gilead
Samaria falls to the Assyrians after a long siege
Sargon II deports some 27,000 people and creates the province of Samerina
Sennacherib invades Judah, takes Lachish and besieges Jerusalem
Josiah’s religious reform centralises worship in Jerusalem
Josiah is killed at Megiddo confronting the pharaoh Necho II
Nebuchadnezzar II captures Jerusalem and deports Jehoiachin
Jerusalem and the temple are destroyed; the elite are exiled to Babylon
The advance of the Islamic State drives Aramaic-speaking Christians from their towns in northern Iraq
Shalmaneser III of Assyria sacks Arzashkun, royal city of King Arame
Argishti I founds the fortress of Erebuni, origin of Yerevan
Tiglath-pileser III defeats Sarduri II and his Syrian allies
Sargon II defeats Rusa I and sacks the temple of Haldi at Musasir
Itamra the Sabaean sends gifts to Sargon II of Assyria
Aelius Gallus besieges Marib for six days and retreats
Cyaxares and Nabopolassar of Babylon destroy Nineveh
War with Lydia ends after the battle of the eclipse, fixing the Halys River frontier
Nabopolassar seizes Babylon and restores native Babylonian kingship
Babylonians and Medes sack Nineveh, the Assyrian capital
Crown prince Nebuchadnezzar II defeats Necho II's Egyptians at Carchemish
Nebuchadnezzar captures Jerusalem and deports King Jehoiachin
Nebuchadnezzar II dies; four kings follow in six years
Cyrus the Great wins at Opis and Babylon falls without real resistance
Cyrus II defeats Astyages and takes over the Median Empire
Cyrus defeats the Babylonians at Opis and enters Babylon
Cambyses II defeats Psamtik III at Pelusium and conquers Egypt
Xerxes invades Greece, wins at Thermopylae, sacks Athens but loses at Salamis
Egypt revolts on the death of Darius II and stays independent for six decades
Alexander the Great defeats Darius III at Gaugamela
Alexander burns Persepolis; Darius III is murdered by his satrap Bessus
The fall of the Sasanian empire to the Arab conquerors makes Arabic the language of government
Death of the poet Rumi, author of the Masnavi
The Mughal emperor Akbar makes Persian the language of all government records in his empire
Persian is replaced by English and local languages as the official language of British India
Seleucus retakes Babylon after the Battle of Gaza, the starting point of the Seleucid era
Seleucus and Lysimachus defeat and kill Antigonus at the Battle of Ipsus
Seleucus defeats Lysimachus at Corupedium but is assassinated within months
Antiochus III begins a seven-year eastern campaign that earns him the title 'the Great'
Rome routs Antiochus III's army at the Battle of Magnesia
Antiochus IV's suppression of Jewish practice sparks the Maccabean revolt
Mithridates I of Parthia conquers Mesopotamia and captures Seleucia-on-Tigris
Pompey deposes Antiochus XIII and makes Syria a Roman province
Pompey invades Iberia and forces King Artoces to submit
Pharasmanes I seizes Armenia for his brother Mithridates
Vespasian fortifies Mtskheta for King Mithridates of Iberia
Vakhtang I Gorgasali joins the Armenian revolt against Persia
Mithridates I Ktistes takes the title of king
Pharnaces I captures Sinope and makes it his capital
Mithridates VI overruns Roman Asia and orders the massacre of Romans and Italians
Peace of Dardanus ends the First Mithridatic War
Pompey routs Mithridates on the Lycus river
Mithridates VI dies at Panticapaeum; Pompey divides Pontus
Yusuf As'ar Yath'ar besieges Najran, where many Christians are killed
Kaleb of Aksum invades, and Yusuf is defeated and killed
Albanians join the Armenian rising crushed at the Battle of Avarayr
Constantine and Licinius grant Christians freedom of worship, the so-called Edict of Milan
The Council of Nicaea, called by Constantine, defines the faith in the Nicene Creed
Theodosius I makes Nicene Christianity the religion of the Roman Empire
The Great Schism divides the Latin West from the Greek East
Martin Luther’s Ninety-five Theses begin the Protestant Reformation
Mani is born in Mesopotamia, near the Persian capital Ctesiphon
The Tang emperor Wuzong bans Manichaeism in China
The image of Mani as the Buddha of Light is carved at Cao’an near Quanzhou
